messages:
Alex K: I'm taking primary for the overnight window (00:00-08:00 UTC). Quick handoff notes below — please ack if you see any gaps.

Alex K: Primary = me, Secondary = Maria S (00:00-04:00 UTC), Backup = Jen N (04:00-08:00 UTC). Sam P is on-call for infra escalations.

Maria S: ack. I can cover 00:00-04:00, but I'll be slow ~02:00-02:30 UTC (calendar). Jen, can you be ready to jump in around 03:45 if needed?

Jen N: yep, I'll stay proximate 03:30 onwards.

oncall-bot: Reminder: runbook quick links for on-call -> https://intra.redwood/runbooks/oncall-index (saved), inference incidents -> https://intra.redwood/runbooks/inference-availability

Alex K: Two quick coverage gaps to call out: (1) No dedicated secondary from 02:00-02:30 UTC (Maria limited), (2) deployment slot for model-x-quant is at risk of hitting capacity if the nightly batch job spikes.

Maria S: For the model-x capacity spike, runbook recommends temporary routing to model-x-fallback (same family but lower throughput). Link in runbook.

Alex K: TL;DR mitigation playbook I expect to use if paging: 1) validate customer impact, 2) scale dedicated pool / bump replicas, 3) route to fallback variant, 4) if control-plane errors, restart runtime pods.

Alex K: Customer impact assessment tips: check the /metrics endpoint for 5xx increase, trace sample queries in Console -> Requests -> Last 30m, and check alert dashboard - use 'inference.latency.p50/p95' and 'inference.errors.5xx' panels. If >3x baseline p95 or error rate >1% start mitigation.

Sam P: If you need to scale quickly, use the dedicated autoscale override: `POST /api/internal/scale?pool=d-ed-01&replicas=+2` (ops role required). I can run it if you ping me.

Alex K: Quick commands saved here if you need to restart the runtime pods (prod cluster):
```
# restart inference runtime rollout
kubectl -n prod rollout restart deployment/inference-runtime
# drain a node quickly (if kernel OOM suspected)
kubectl drain ip-xx-yy --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```

Maria S: If the incident is model-specific (model-x), prefer soft-fallback first: update routing weight to fallback 100% via the routing console or CLI: `redwood route update --model model-x --fallback model-x-fallback --weight 100`

Jen N: Runbook pointer for pager flow (bookmark): https://intra.redwood/runbooks/pager-flow — contains checklist: Acknowledge, Assess, Mitigate, Communicate, Postmortem. Keep status updates every 10-15m when paging.

incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: inference.errors.5xx spike detected for prod/model-x at 2026-03-14T02:07:30Z — firing 3/5 rules. Pager sent to @oncall-primary.

Alex K: I see the alert. Checking dashboards now. First glance: p95 latency x3 and 5xxs concentrated on model-x CPU OOMs on a single node.

Alex K: Mitigation plan in order: 1) move traffic off node via `kubectl cordon`+`drain` if node failing, 2) scale pool up temporarily, 3) route to fallback if scaling doesn't drop errors.

Sam P: I'm at laptop. If you ask, I'll scale the pool and watch infra metrics.

Maria S: While Alex does validation, I'll prepare the routing change. If we switch to fallback, remember to lower batch_window to avoid throughput blowouts.

Alex K: Running a quick log sample: `kubectl logs inference-runtime-57f9 -n prod | grep OOM` — seeing repeated OOM kills. Will cordon/drain the node now.

Alex K: Executed drain, pods are rescheduling. Watching for stability (10m).

oncall-bot: Deploys in last 1h: model-x-serving v1.12 (canary) — check if canary rollout coincides. https://intra.redwood/deploys/last-hour

Maria S: I pushed a routing change to send 30% to fallback while we validate: `redwood route update --model model-x --fallback model-x-fallback --weight 30` — monitoring.

Alex K: After drain + 30% fallback: errors down ~60% and p95 improving. Recommend full fallback to 100% for next 15 minutes while we confirm.

Jen N: I'll take over primary at 04:00 UTC. Alex, please leave notes in the incident channel and set a short post-incident eval runbook task: check cache warming and KV cache hitrate after fallback.

Alex K: Will do. Leaving the following quick checklist for whoever picks this up: - Confirm errors stable for 15m - If stable, rollback routing gradually back to model-x in 10% increments every 5m - Run `redis-cli --stat` check for KV cache pressure - Open a ticket linking the canary deploy that appears suspicious: infra-ticket #TODO

Maria S: Noted. Also add action: update the model onboarding doc with memory/oom heuristics for quantized variants.

Jen N: ack. I'll monitor until 04:00 and then hand over to Sam for infra follow-up if needed.

Alex K: Final notes and links: runbook (inference availability): https://intra.redwood/runbooks/inference-availability, pager flow: https://intra.redwood/runbooks/pager-flow, routing CLI quick reference: https://intra.redwood/docs/routing-cli.

Sam P: thanks all. If you see any unresolved node defects after reschedule, tag me and I'll open an infra ticket.

Alex K: thanks team. Leaving Slack status: `oncall:primary` and a short pinned checklist in the incident channel. :thumbsup:
